parsed.rationale: The pipeline reports a Jaccard similarity of 0.75 between `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477), both in `WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift` in the `app:iOS` package. The high overlap strongly suggests the two methods share the same navigation logic and differ only in the direction of traversal. Neither method carries any context flags (`is_test`, `is_codegen`, `is_mock`, `is_sample_app` are all false), so the duplication is not intentional by policy. Introducing a direction parameter collapses the shared body into one place, reducing future maintenance risk when the theme-navigation logic changes.

specifics.proposed_action: Unify `WXYCApp.navigateToPreviousTheme` (line 465) and `WXYCApp.navigateToNextTheme` (line 477) in `WXYC/iOS/WXYCApp.swift` into a single private helper method — e.g., `navigateTheme(direction: ThemeNavigationDirection)` or `navigateTheme(offset: Int)` — where the direction/offset parameter encodes whether to step backward or forward. Both call sites become one-liners that pass `.previous`/`.next` (or `-1`/`+1`). This eliminates the near-duplicate body (Jaccard 0.75) while keeping the two public entry-point names as thin forwarding wrappers if they are part of a public API surface, or by replacing them entirely if they are internal.
